To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the more financial partners in a World Bank project, the lower its performance rating, and that this is especially true when the project is funded by a single donor.
projects with significant co-financing are more likely to have lower overall project ratings than projects with little co-financing.
projects with more funding streams receive worse project ratings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the division of funding in World Bank projects on project effectiveness.
the question of whether or not too many cooks in the kitchen reduce the effectiveness of aid projects.
the effects of the division of financing in World Bank projects on project effectiveness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more funding partners a project has, the more likely it is to be less effective.
the more actors there are involved in the financing of a project the lower is its overall performance.
projects that have many funding streams are more likely to receive a worse project rating, but the effect is small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
projects with multiple funding sources have lower effectiveness ratings, but this relationship is not robust to different specifications or sample restrictions.
there is no evidence that projects with more funding streams are more likely to be successful than projects with fewer.
there is some evidence that projects with more funding sources are less successful, and that this is likely due to a combination of increased transaction costs and unclear accountability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of financial collaborators is a good indicator of a project’s complexity and, thus, of its potential for poor performance.
the World Bank should take steps to reduce the number of financial collaborators in projects and to encourage the use of fewer, larger, more concentrated funding streams.
the division of funding among multiple actors is a factor to be taken into consideration when evaluating project effectiveness.
